alt: A Sun at left sends arrows rightward toward Earth and four Moon positions; every small Moon has its left half illuminated.
Eight disks form two rows: dark, right crescent, right half, right gibbous; full, left gibbous, left half, left crescent.
A thin pale crescent follows the right rim of a dark circular Moon against navy.
A mostly pale circular Moon has a narrow dark region along its left rim.
Three Moon disks progress from a right-lit crescent to a right-lit half and a right-lit gibbous.

The Sun, Earth and a small copper Moon align from left to right; a narrowing dark region extends from Earth around the Moon.
Earth blocks light from a Sun at left, leaving a dark narrowing region containing a small Moon to its right.
Four Moon positions circle Earth; a golden surface marker on each Moon is turned inward toward Earth.
